newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on on weather, soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on on weather, soybeans.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a drop in soybeans plus Midwest weather which was deemed conducive for crop production, traders said.

Recent rainfall in the Midwest and warmer temperatures have boosted prospects for 1997 U.S. corn production, traders said. The market was expecting the U.S. corn crop to show an improvement in condition ratings in Monday's USDA weekly state crop briefs.
Routine exports also were cited. USDA's weekly export inspections report showed corn inspected for exporting during the week ended June 5 at 22.885 million bushels.
That tally was near the low end of expectations for 22.0 million to 28.0 million bushels.
Farmers Commodities Corp sold two million bushels of December, ADM Investor Services sold two million July and sold one million December, traders said.
LIT America sold three million December and Cargill Inc sold three million December, traders said.
Smith Barney bought three million bushels of July and sold three million December, traders said.
Corn closed unchanged to 1-3/4 cents lower, with July unchanged at $2.74.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 57,000 contracts, above the 38,720 traded Friday.

In corn options, O'Connor and Co bought 300 December $3.10 calls at 4-1/2 to 4-3/8 cents, Farmers Commodities Corp sold 225 September $2.60 calls at 11-1/2 to 12 cents and E.D. and F. Man International bought 500 December $2.70 calls at 11 cents and sold 500 December $3.00 calls at 5-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 13,000 contracts, above the 10,100 traded Friday.
